descriptionChirho: The preposition עִם with first-person singular suffix expressing accompaniment, association, or proximity: 'with me.' This is the dominant sense (41 of 44 occurrences). Multilingual evidence: English 'with me,' Spanish 'conmigo,' Hindi मेरे साथ / मुझसे ('with me / from me'), Arabic مَعِي / عِنْدِي ('with me / at my place'), Korean 나와 함께 ('together with me'), Swahili pamoja nami / nami ('together with me'). Covers comitative, sociative, and proximity uses of this common preposition.

The compound prepositional expression מֵעִמָּדִי (מִן + עִם + 1cs), meaning 'from with me' or 'away from my presence,' indicating separation from a person's company or domain. English 'from with me,' Spanish 'de con mí / de conmigo,' Hindi मुझसे ('from me'), Arabic مِنْ عِنْدِي ('from my place/presence'), Korean 나에게서 ('from me'), Swahili kutoka kwangu ('from my place'). The addition of the separative preposition מִן creates a distinct ablative sense not present in the simple comitative עִמָּדִי.

The preposition עִם with first-person singular suffix used reflexively, meaning 'with myself' or 'within myself,' expressing internal deliberation or self-communion. English 'with myself,' Spanish 'conmigo' (reflexive context), Hindi अपने आप से ('with one's own self'), Arabic في نَفْسي ('in myself'), Korean 나 자신 안에서 ('within myself'), Swahili ndani yangu ('inside me'). This reflexive use is semantically distinct from the comitative sense, pointing inward rather than toward another person.
